lessons.title: 9. 气体、液体和固体的结构

nearbyText: Molecular kinetic theory helps explain why matter can exist as a gas, a liquid, or a solid.

Gases: In the usual dilute-gas approximation, the average distance between atoms or molecules is much greater than the size of a molecule (Figure $6$).
The source gives an order-of-magnitude example: at $1$ atmosphere, the container volume is tens of thousands of times the total volume assigned to its gas molecules.
This ratio also depends on temperature, the gas, and how molecular volume is estimated.
